_note: Values transcribed from the NASA LSDA files in Data_Set.zip (AP005 tables converted from .xls, AP005 figures/PDFs, DSO 484 table). Group means as published; p = significance of the first postflight evaluation vs preflight.

apollo.source: NASA LSDA AP005 - Apollo Flight Crew Cardiovascular Evaluations (Hoffler & Johnson, NASA SP-368, 1975). Apollo 7-17, mission length 6.0 to 12.6 days.
apollo.recoveryByThirdEval: Resting heart rate was back to 63.5 bpm (not significant vs preflight) at the third postflight evaluation.

oralTempVsRestingHr.text: Change in oral temperature vs change in resting heart rate: r = 0.27, NOT significant, n = 24 (about +10 % resting heart rate per +1 degC).

calfVsWeightlessness.text: Calf size decreased more the longer the crew were weightless (r = -0.47, p < 0.025, n = 24): fluid shifts toward the head.

figures.weightLoss: Apollo and Gemini crews lost body weight in flight and the loss levelled off after about 200 hours.
figures.cardiothoracicRatio: Chest X-rays showed a smaller heart (cardiothoracic ratio decreased) after flight, consistent with cardiovascular deconditioning.

sts46.source: NASA LSDA DSO 484 (Putcha). Whitson PA, Putcha L, Chen YM, Baker E. J Pineal Res 1995;18(3):141-7.
sts46.design: 7-day bright-light / sleep-shifting protocol, 8 subjects (three sleep-shift protocols A, B, C).
sts46.note: Only 5 of 8 subjects have a salivary melatonin result. Several other cells in the table lost their decimal point (for example 169 for 16.9), so only the clean salivary melatonin column is used.

inspiration4.source: NASA OSDR OSD-575 / OSD-569 (LSDS-8): SpaceX Inspiration4, 3-day mission, September 2021, 4 crew (C001-C004). Samples preflight L-92, L-44, L-3 and post-flight R+1, R+45, R+82, R+194 (days).
inspiration4.limits: Only 4 people and 3 days in orbit: results show direction and size of change, not statistics.
